questions.q: What does periodic backup mode do by default?
options: Automatically takes full backups at a configurable interval (default every 4 hours) and retains a configurable number of recent backups
Continuously streams every write to a backup store in real time
Requires the DBA to manually trigger every backup
Backs up data once per year
questions.explain: Periodic backup is Cosmos DB's default/legacy mode, taking discrete snapshots on a schedule rather than continuously.

questions.q: What does restoring from a periodic backup restore to?
options: One of the discrete snapshot points, into a new account — not an arbitrary moment in time
Any exact second within a 30-day window
The original account, in place, overwriting current data
A different Azure subscription entirely, automatically
questions.explain: Periodic backup restore is limited to the coarse snapshot points that were taken, and it creates a new account rather than restoring in place.

questions.q: What does continuous backup mode enable that periodic backup mode cannot?
options: Point-in-time restore (PITR) to any specific timestamp within the retention window
Automatic multi-region writes
Free storage for all backups regardless of retention
Encryption at rest for the first time
questions.explain: Continuous backup continuously captures data changes, allowing restore to any second in the retention window — not just fixed snapshot points.

questions.q: Why does the distinction between periodic and continuous backup genuinely matter, per this lesson?
options: Recovering precisely before an incident (like a bad deploy or accidental bulk delete) requires the fine-grained restore only continuous backup provides
There is no real functional difference — it's purely a pricing label
Periodic backup is always faster to restore than continuous backup
Continuous backup does not support self-service restore
questions.explain: The lesson frames this as the core practical difference: precise recovery points matter when an incident happens between periodic snapshots.

questions.q: How long is the retention window for continuous backup mode?
options: 7 or 30 days, depending on the tier
Exactly 4 hours, matching periodic backup's interval
Indefinitely, with no maximum retention
1 hour only
questions.explain: Continuous backup's point-in-time restore is bounded by a 7-day or 30-day retention window depending on the selected tier.
